AI Build Limited (t/a Aibuild) is a London-based software company specialising in computer-aided manufacturing and AI automation for industrial additive manufacturing. Founded in 2015, we develop software used at over 100 industrial customers worldwide for process planning, simulation, and autonomous toolpath generation across directed energy deposition (DED), wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM), and other AM processes.
Our core product, Aibuild CAM, is a machine-agnostic platform that programs, simulates, optimizes, and generates machine instruction files for robotic and gantry AM systems. It includes Aibuild FETS, a GPU-accelerated finite element thermal solver built specifically for metal AM, and an AI Agent that autonomously generates toolpaths, runs quality checks, and iterates without user intervention. In March 2026, we extended this with Aibuild OS: a multi-agent AI platform that connects CAD, FEA, and CAM tools into autonomous engineering workflows driven by natural language prompts.
We maintain an active physical R&D programme at our London lab, which houses six robotic systems including a Fronius WAAM cell. This facility provides continuous process validation and training data for our software. AI Build Limited is ISO 27001 certified and supports ITAR-compatible local deployment for regulated environments.

description:
Vimotek — Controlled spacecraft encounters from validation to orbit
Vimotek is a European space technology company helping mission teams turn spacecraft encounters into controlled, predictable outcomes.
As orbital density increases and proximity operations become more central to future missions, operators need to validate encounter logic before flight, execute rendezvous and close-proximity operations in orbit, and assess uncertain proximity behaviour with confidence.
Vimotek builds productised capabilities across two complementary domains: mission-specific digital twins for simulation and validation, and onboard sensing and perception.
Orbittwin — digital twin platform and mission environment for modelling, validation, rehearsal and operational decision support.
Navcam — RPO system for onboard target acquisition, tracking and characterisation during mission encounters.
Sentinel — SSA system for onboard detection, monitoring and assessment of nearby objects and anomalous proximity behaviour.

Prometheus Plasma Systems S.r.l. is a deep-tech company developing a novel plasma-based configuration that merges the functional capabilities of turbomachinery with the extreme, controllable conditions enabled by plasma physics. This configuration forms the basis of a broad, modular technological platform applicable across high-vacuum systems, plasma processing, advanced radiation sources, electric space propulsion, and—longer term—nuclear fusion technologies.
Rather than addressing a single product category, Prometheus Plasma Systems (PPS) targets a class of systemic limitations shared by many advanced industries: the difficulty of operating reliably, efficiently, and economically in extreme environments where conventional mechanical, electromagnetic, or thermal solutions face intrinsic constraints. These limitations appear in different forms across sectors—mechanical wear and contamination in vacuum systems, power-supply inefficiencies in plasma propulsion, lack of flexible and affordable plasma diagnostics, and escalating complexity and cost in fusion reactor concepts—but stem from a common root: architectures that are not designed to fully exploit plasma as an active, controllable medium.
PPS aims to address structural inefficiencies in two high-value sectors: industrial turbomachinery—where system complexity, high capital costs, and intensive maintenance constrain growth—and plasma and nuclear fusion technologies, where over-engineered architectures and extreme costs confine applications largely to research environments.
Our mission is to introduce a new class of turbomachines that operate with plasma as the working fluid and eliminate mechanical power transfer entirely. By replacing rotating and mechanically coupled components with electromagnetic energy transfer systems, PPS removes all moving parts from the core architecture. The result is a fundamentally simpler, modular, and stackable platform with significantly reduced mechanical wear, lower maintenance requirements, enhanced scalability and lower costs.
This no-moving-part turbomachinery approach unlocks a whole new paradigm in high-performance fluid systems, enabling broader industrial adoption through improved reliability, lower lifecycle costs, and adaptable integration across multiple advanced technology sectors.

Serenity Corporation is a French SAS founded in 2024, headquartered in Cannes, specializing in the design, manufacture, and commercialization of autonomous Atmospheric Water Generators (AWGs). These eco-designed, modular systems extract humidity from the air to produce pure drinking water, without relying on public infrastructure, piping, or plastic distribution.
Serenity offers a product range from S10 to custom industrial models (up to 10,000 L/day), with configurations adapted for indoor, outdoor, and extreme environments. Each unit follows a five-stage process—capturing, condensing, filtering, disinfecting (UV), and mineralizing water.
The company’s innovation lies in its dual-use approach:
Terrestrial: Providing decentralized, sustainable water solutions to hotels, eco-lodges, coworking spaces, municipalities, and NGOs.

Space: Adapting AWG systems for closed-loop space habitats and developing AI-powered climate forecasting software integrating Copernicus satellite data with local sensor networks.

Serenity also delivers Serenity Care subscription services, IoT modules, maintenance, and leasing. Backed by BFTE funding and in application for ESA BIC Sud France, Serenity collaborates with partners such as INPHYNI (CNRS/UCA), IMREDD, Somanity, Hautier IP, and Spartan Space to advance R&D, industrialization, and intellectual property protection.
